parameter: R&D and Clinical Evidence for Lactoferrin
gap: Based on primary research, the company has not disclosed a dedicated clinical trial timeline or specific annual budget allocations designated for lactoferrin-exclusive R&D initiatives.
object: a dedicated clinical trial timeline or specific annual budget allocations designated for lactoferrin-exclusive R&D initiatives
findings: A collaborative in vitro study published in 2022 by the University of Michigan and Glanbia Research and Development demonstrated that bovine lactoferrin supplied by Glanbia Nutritionals successfully inhibited SARS-CoV-2 variant cell entry and supported host antiviral defenses.

Glanbia Nutritionals' bovine lactoferrin has been evaluated in a third-party prospective, dose-escalation clinical safety study involving preterm infants, proving to be well-tolerated with zero solution-related adverse events across 30 days of enteral administration.

The assessment is based on the company's verified provision of proprietary bovine lactoferrin (Bioferrin) for third-party clinical safety trials and its joint participation in published in vitro efficacy research exploring broad antiviral properties.
